keyVerseText: And he answered and said, He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.
rootMeaning: The Greek noun τρύβλιον (trýblion) is a neuter term whose precise etymology is uncertain, but it denotes a physical vessel such as a bowl or dish. Its core meaning centers on a container used for holding or serving food or drink, which is more tangible and concrete than the general English word "dish." This literal sense emphasizes the object's function as a receptacle, often associated with communal sharing or measurement in ancient contexts.
usageInScripture: The word τρύβλιον appears only twice in Scripture, consistently translated as "the dish." This limited but focused usage highlights its specific reference to a particular kind of bowl or cup, underscoring its role as a physical object rather than a metaphorical concept. The consistency of translation reveals that the term is employed to identify a concrete item involved in significant narrative moments, reinforcing its tangible presence within the biblical text.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding τρύβλιον as a concrete dish deepens our appreciation for the physical realities present in the Gospel narratives, reminding us that God chose to reveal Himself within ordinary, everyday objects and moments. This word anchors spiritual truth in tangible elements, reflecting the incarnation whereby divine truth is communicated through material means. Moreover, the communal aspect implied by sharing from a dish points to the fellowship and intimacy central to Christian faith, as believers are called to partake together in the life of Christ. Recognizing the literal vessel also prepares us to grasp the gravity of betrayal occurring within such a shared, sacred setting.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 26:23, Jesus says, "He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me," highlighting the intimate act of sharing from the same τρύβλιον. The word "dish" here is not merely a background detail but a symbol of fellowship and trust, making the impending betrayal all the more poignant. The physical sharing of the dish underscores the closeness between Jesus and His disciples, intensifying the shock of the treachery that will come from one so near.
